segments.text: Early JWST candidates appeared too numerous and too massive for standard simulations. This paper asks a narrower question: does the observed abundance exceed IllustrisTNG by more than the stellar-mass systematic budget?
Above ten to the 10.5 solar masses, observations give about three times ten to the minus five galaxies per cubic megaparsec. TNG gives 1.1 times ten to the minus five: a factor 2.7 difference.

Because the simulated high-mass tail is steep, shifting the observed stellar masses downward by only 0.28 dex removes the redshift five-to-six excess. Recent analyses allow a systematic budget near one dex.

Photometric candidates at redshifts seven to nine also move inside the broad mass budget in the paper's headline calculation. But spectroscopically confirmed quiescent galaxies above redshift six remain about two dex over-predicted and unresolved.

The result does not confirm Lambda CDM. It says the current redshift-five-to-six massive-galaxy counts do not require new physics once realistic stellar-mass systematics are allowed. The quiescent population needs separate follow-up.

The masses, candidate confirmation, and simulated volume all limit this comparison. This is a machine-generated descriptive draft, not a validated measurement. Automated review is not journal or human peer review.
